checks.name: R1 required headers
checks.why: the listing will not build without these

checks.name: R2 stable tag is the shipped version
checks.why: a stable tag that is not the version in the file ships the wrong code

checks.name: R3 requires at least agrees with the code
checks.why: two places state the same minimum

checks.name: R4 requires php agrees with the code
checks.why: same

checks.name: R5 tested up to is the newest version we ran on
checks.why: evidence/verify-<version>.json records a full pass on that WordPress

checks.name: R24 requires at least is the oldest version we ran on
checks.why: a minimum nobody tried is a guess, and this one was run: 24/24 on 6.0.3 with PHP 7.4.32

checks.name: R6 short description length
checks.why: WordPress.org truncates over 150 characters, and a cut sentence reads as sloppy

checks.name: R7 at most five tags
checks.why: only the first five are used

checks.name: R8 required sections
checks.why: the listing tabs come from these

checks.name: R9 changelog covers the stable tag
checks.why: a release with no changelog entry

checks.name: R10 one caption per screenshot file
checks.why: an uncaptioned image, or a caption for an image that is not in the zip

checks.name: R11 the screenshot is the one we took
checks.why: the picture came from a real admin screen that answered 200

checks.name: R12 the screenshot file is the one measured
checks.why: the recorded hash has to belong to the file that ships

checks.name: R13 caption counts the figures that are there
checks.why: the caption describes the picture, and the picture is the screen

checks.name: R14 the privacy claim holds in the code
checks.why: guideline 7: the readme says it cannot talk out, so the names must be absent

checks.name: R15 nothing is for sale in the code
checks.why: guideline 5: the readme says everything is free

checks.name: R16 post ceiling in the faq
checks.why: the number a buyer plans around

checks.name: R17 batch size in the installation steps
checks.why: same

checks.name: R18 the stored option is the one named
checks.why: the readme tells people what to delete

checks.name: R19 the capability the faq promises
checks.why: the readme says who can see the report

checks.name: R27 the faq answer on who can see it was measured
checks.why: a capability named in the source is not a refusal anyone observed; evidence/verify-<version>.json has to show a logged in non administrator being turned away and the scan not running for them

checks.name: R28 the plugin uri was opened and answered
checks.why: a header url nobody fetched can be a 404; evidence/plugin_uri.json has to show a 200 for this exact url with the repository name in the page

checks.name: R20 text domain matches the slug
checks.why: translations load by slug on WordPress.org

checks.name: R21 every translatable string is in the pot
checks.why: a string missing from the pot can never be translated

checks.name: R22 the pot carries the right domain
checks.why: wrong domain in the pot means the translations never load

checks.name: R25 the zip holds the files as they are now
checks.why: a zip built before the last edit submits code nobody checked

checks.name: R26 the zip carries the required files
checks.why: readme.txt and the main file are what the reviewer opens

checks.name: R29 the published download was fetched and matches the zip
checks.why: the readme tells people to install from the releases page; evidence/release_asset.json has to show a logged out download of that exact zip, from a published release whose tag serves the same four files

checks.name: R23 no em dash in the listing
checks.why: house style: an em dash is the surface marker we remove everywhere else
